issues.description: The validation report's differential run shows the golden/expert submission fails preflight because submission/vulnerability_report.json is not valid JSON at the time evaluate.py runs (JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1). This means either the golden expert file was not properly placed at the expected submission path during grading, or the golden content itself is malformed/empty. Either way, the evaluator rejects a correct submission, which is disqualifying for this benchmark.
issues.evidence: golden_run.stdout: "[TEST] FAIL: SETUP: submission/vulnerability_report.json is not valid JSON: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)"

issues.description: Because the golden run errors out at SETUP before any FR/SR checks execute, none of the required requirement IDs (FR1-FR4, SR1-SR4) ever get a [TEST] PASS/FAIL line on the golden run, causing a requirement_id_mismatch against the requirement_map. The evaluator's marker IDs are only exercised on the baseline (naive) run, not on a correct submission, so there's no evidence the evaluator actually accepts a correct report.
issues.evidence: issues: requirement_id_mismatch: "evaluate.py never emitted [TEST] PASS/FAIL for ['FR1','FR2','FR3','FR4','SR1','SR2','SR3','SR4'] on the golden run"

issues.description: mutation_status is blocked_by_differential and mutation_score_meaningful is false, meaning no confidence has been established that the evaluator can discriminate between correct and incorrect/vulnerable submissions across mutations. requirement_discrimination_coverage_score is 0.0.

The submission_invariants section shows baseline and golden sha256 differ and mappings are marked 'changed': true with status pass, but this does not resolve the core golden-run failure documented in the differential section — the invariants check and differential check appear inconsistent (invariants imply the golden file is present and differs from baseline, yet the differential run reports the file as unparsable JSON).

recommendations: Fix the golden/expert submission file or the test harness so that submission/vulnerability_report.json actually exists and is valid JSON at the path evaluate.py reads when grading the golden run; the differential preflight must show the golden run passing (exit 0, all PASS lines for FR1-FR4/SR1-SR4) before this benchmark can be considered usable.

Re-run the differential check after fixing the golden placement issue and confirm exit_code 0 for the golden run and non-zero for the naive baseline run, with matching PASS/FAIL lines for every requirement ID in requirement_map.

Increase confidence in SR2's parser robustness: the regex-based linear-formula parser is fragile (e.g., may fail on legitimate paraphrased formulas like 'two plus the index of the first differing byte'); consider more robust parsing or accept multiple explicit per-case cycle values in addition to a formula.

Run mutation testing (e.g., flipping the fix description to omit one of the three SR3 elements, or reporting a plausible but incorrect off-by-two formula for SR2) to raise requirement_discrimination_coverage_score above 0 and confirm the evaluator actually distinguishes near-miss submissions from fully correct ones.

Verify that the golden report's early_exit_signal, cycle_relationship, and constant_time_fix strings actually satisfy the regex patterns in check_sr1/check_sr2/check_sr3 by testing them directly against evaluate.py in isolation, independent of the submission-path issue, to rule out a second latent bug in the semantic-matching regexes.
